scene.name: NeoTokyo_Vertical_Megastructure

origin.meaning: center of city and rotation axis

vertical_modules.seam_rule: logical partitions only; continuous geometry must not terminate at boundaries

scene.design_status: initial technical baseline; dimensions are project defaults, not measurements inferred from source photos

modules.notes: supports, utility corridors, tanks, ducts, service platforms; no flat ground cap
industrial structures transition into denser blocks
transit decks, bridges, dense commercial blocks
primary billboards, skybridges, major tower facades
tall tower bodies, antenna supports, elevated links
spires, antennae, rooftop machinery and skyline silhouettes

objects.name: Slide spire (presentation tower)
objects.shape: octagonal core of radius 1.6 m inside a four-leg braced lattice of radius 2.6 m, Z=-144..+114; collar rings halfway between slides; stepped crown +114..+131 with two decks, equipment pods, dishes and three lattice masts to +166, needle to +128 below the logo point +136
details: 13 slim cantilever mounts on a helix
dark collar ring with a junction box, monitor and landing between every two slides
two recessed cyan seams on the core
conduits with clamps on two lattice legs, red leg lights every third collar
objects.placement: city axis; the only structure inside the camera shaft besides designated bridges
objects.optimization: single silhouette mesh; mounts exported as empties MOUNT-01..13 for the browser

objects.name: Primary spine tower
objects.shape: asymmetric stepped shaft with three setbacks, exposed frame on one side, narrow antenna crown
details: cyan vertical display on one face
objects.placement: outer or middle band; exact sector coordinate is a blockout decision
objects.optimization: separate silhouette mesh, instanced facade grid, LOD for window details

objects.name: Needle tower
objects.shape: narrow tapered upper 30 percent, two service rings, antenna mast
objects.placement: different sector from TWR-01 to preserve silhouette variety

objects.name: Stepped slab tower
objects.shape: offset blocks, cantilevered decks and an exposed side truss
objects.placement: middle band; must have detailed rear and side faces

objects.name: Ring crown tower
objects.shape: cylindrical core with two exterior ring platforms
objects.placement: alternate between inner and outer bands
objects.optimization: low-sided ring geometry for distant LOD

objects.name: Mid-rise urban block
objects.shape: reusable rectilinear volume with balconies, window bands and service bays
objects.placement: fill gaps between towers without creating a continuous wall

objects.name: Dense commercial block
objects.shape: layered signage, overhangs and narrow vertical service shafts

objects.name: Industrial utility block
objects.shape: dense low-rise service building with tanks and vents
objects.optimization: combine small fixed props into a few meshes

objects.name: Enclosed skybridge
objects.shape: enclosed walkway with structural frame and maintenance mounts
objects.placement: connect real facade support points; span may vary 18–42 m

objects.name: Open catwalk
objects.shape: grated walkway with rails and cross-bracing
objects.placement: short service connections and facade maintenance routes

objects.name: Elevated transit deck
objects.shape: deck with support beams, edge barriers and modular straight/curved pieces
objects.placement: multiple elevation bands; vary route direction
objects.optimization: reuse track/deck segments and hide unseen faces

objects.name: Standard facade module
objects.shape: window group, panel frame and optional service strip
objects.placement: grid on compatible tower and block surfaces

objects.name: Corner facade module
objects.shape: two-plane corner wrap with aligned sill and top frame

objects.name: Billboard assembly
objects.shape: display plane, rigid frame and rear maintenance access
objects.placement: major facades; not every building gets a billboard
objects.optimization: one texture atlas per sign family; avoid transparent stacks

objects.name: Rooftop equipment pack
objects.shape: fan housings, vents, antenna bases and conduits

objects.name: Utility pipe bundle
objects.shape: three to six pipes with broad bends and brackets every 3–5 m
details: avoid high-sided circular geometry at long distances
objects.placement: tower exteriors and lower service corridors
objects.optimization: curve geometry at close range; simplified mesh for LOD

objects.name: Emissive facade strip
objects.shape: thin plane or low-sided strip; use a real profile only where silhouette matters
details: local variations rather than continuous full-building glow
objects.placement: selected facade edges and sign frames
objects.optimization: combine into emissive atlases where possible

materials.name: M_DarkMetal
materials.use: main structural panels and tower frames

materials.name: M_TintedGlass
materials.use: opaque dark glass; avoid alpha blending where possible

materials.name: M_CyanEmission
materials.use: major cyan strips and selected screens

materials.name: M_AmberEmission
materials.use: windows, work lights and service beacons

materials.name: M_AsphaltWet
materials.use: wet hero floors with roughness variation

materials.name: M_TechPolymer
materials.use: vent housings, service doors and technical plastic

local_sign_lights.purpose: selective local bounce near hero signs

lighting.principle: use emissive surfaces as primary visible neon; do not create one real light per sign
lighting.browser_note: Blender-only bloom/compositor and Eevee effects are not guaranteed in glTF; reimplement glow in the target renderer

hero.purpose: vertical hero render with foreground infrastructure
hero.note_r1: moved from (0,-108,-20) to clear the outer band; HERO-DECK platform gives the foreground railing

descent.purpose: validate scene rotation and downward movement
descent.note_r1: moved from radius 118 to 150: the rotating city reaches radius 124

connections.rule: each bridge endpoint must touch an identified support face or be explicitly cantilevered
connections.validation: inspect both ends in perspective and orthographic renders

connections.rule: major shafts, facade ribs, cable runs and pipes should continue through module boundary bands
4 m facade modules align to common floor datums and consistent pivot points
connections.validation: compare top, bottom and corner edges

connections.rule: all 12 angular sectors contain meaningful architecture and at least two depth layers
vertical module boundaries do not create a visible floor, cap or empty gap

references.authority: zone reference, not stitched continuity proof

references.purpose: cutaway, depth bands and modular studies
building modules and bridge form language

references.authority: concept sheet; create exact views from final Blender meshes
visual-only material reference; values are in materials array

practices: avoid tiny geometry below a few screen pixels
optimization.lod_policy: prefer separate verified LOD exports or a target-engine LOD system; do not assume universal MSFT_lod support

export.materials: Principled BSDF metallic-roughness compatible; pack textures and verify emissive/base-color maps

slide_mounts.angle_convention: slide i sits at Z = top - i*spacing and azimuth a = i*turn, measured from +X towards -Y (three.js: from +X towards +Z after glTF Y-up conversion); the card faces outward along (cos a, -sin a, 0)
slide_mounts.camera_clearance: the presentation camera stays within radius 40 m; no geometry between radius 5 m and 44 m except slide mounts and open bridges on the side opposite the helix

previous.reason: slides of the QA Platform presentation are mounted on a central tower; the camera orbits it inside the shaft, so the shaft is widened and the city is moved outward
changes: inner viewing shaft radius 14 -> 44 m; max radius 92 -> 124 m
new object TWR-00 slide spire and section slide_mounts
hero camera (0,-108,-20) -> (0,-142,-20); descent camera radius 118 -> 150 m
Blender lights: broad key and fill are sun lights; area lights of 600/180 W do not reach across a 248 m city (inverse-square falloff)

facade window variation uses four tiling facade materials M_Facade_* with base and emissive textures, and signs use two glyph atlases M_SignAtlas_*; both derived from M_CoatedPanel / M_TintedGlass and the emission presets
